items.content_html:
Despite existing checks made to ensure gettext is not present on musl, it ended up being unconditionally added to the closure by the patching steps. This PR makes related patches be fully skipped on musl instead.

Note: building git as-is on musl will fail on sqlite tests; that is a combination of missing sanitisers (libasan or libubsan) and a recent sqlite commit ensuring test failures actively fail the entire build as well.

items.content_html:
The release tarball that Nixpkgs uses to build Git includes a pre-generated configure file which isn't committed to the Git source code repositories themselves. Passing the path to curl-config using a configure flag only works when that pre-generated configure file already exists.

Instead of setting the path to curl-config with a slightly obscure configure flag, include it in nativeBuildInputs so it gets picked up both by Nixpkgs' builds using release tarballs, and also in circumstances where src refers a source that doesn't include the pre-generated configure file. This allows downstream users to override the Nixpkgs git package to reference, say, the tip of upstream Git's "next" branch.

This commit is cherry-picked from an unmerged commit that was originally included in #567961.

items.content_html:
Resolves: #560314

Prior to __strictDeps Git's own setup/build would provide a variant of libintl.h that would propagate itself to $out. That unintentional side effect disappeared after and the internationalization support it provided dropped with it. This change ships it explicitly when nlsSupport evals to true.

I verified this on my aarch64-darwin machine which returned the locales directory in $out/share after this was applied where it was missing prior.

items.title: git-pages.services.default: add expiration support

items.content_html:
Description of changes

This makes it possible to include git commit and tag signature verification when using fetchgit.

The motivation for this is to enable maintainers to ensure an update to the source code was authorized by the developers.
As signing keys are supposed to stay the same over multiple versions, they should remain unchanged when updating to a new revision of a given source code.

The verification is done in a non-fixed-output derivation so it will always be executed.
See https://landweber.xyz/ba.pdf Section 5.1.5 and #43233 (comment).

The pr mimics the behaviior of the verified-fetches experimental feature introduced by NixOS/nix#8848.

items.content_html:
Buzz is Block's open-source, Nostr-based workspace for team chat, git hosting and AI agents. buzz-cli is already in nixpkgs. This PR bumps it and adds four more tools from the same Rust workspace. They take their source from buzz-cli (inherit (buzz-cli) version src cargoHash;), so buzz-cli's updateScript keeps all five in step.

  • buzz-cli: 0.1.0-unstable-2026-09-02 -> 0.1.0-unstable-2026-10-03, and adds an updateScript.
  • buzz-agent: an ACP agent that talks to LLM providers and uses MCP tools.
  • buzz-dev-mcp: an MCP server with developer tools (files, shell, search).
  • git-credential-nostr: a git credential helper that signs NIP-98 auth headers.
  • git-sign-nostr: signs git commits and tags with Nostr keys (NIP-GS).

Patches and test skips, each linked upstream:

  • git-sign-nostr and buzz-dev-mcp patch BIP-340 key validation, which broke with nostr 0.44 (block/buzz#6175, fix in block/buzz#8031).
  • buzz-agent skips two racy tests (fix in block/buzz#8091) and one test that clears the environment, so it loses the CA bundle.

Tests: each package has a passthru.tests smoke test that runs offline in the sandbox. They cover the ACP and MCP initialize handshakes, a signed NIP-98 git credential, and a signed commit that git verifies as good:

nix-build -A buzz-agent.tests -A buzz-dev-mcp.tests -A git-credential-nostr.tests -A git-sign-nostr.tests
